gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named reviewer's measured wired-versus-2.4 GHz latency for a Hall effect or TMR board: HLPlanet's OSLTT test of the Gamakay TK75 TMR gave 0.60 ms wired and 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz.
standout_why: I could not open the cited Attack Shark X65 Pro HE and X68 Pro HE pages: attackshark.com returned HTTP 429 on four tries and storecheck returned HTTP 0, and the manuals.plus X68PRO HE manual PDF came back as unreadable binary. The comparison therefore rests on what ChatGPT's answer relayed from those pages (8,000 Hz wired dropping to 1,000 Hz wireless) and on the result titles, all maker product pages, store listings and manuals. Nothing in either answer carries a third-party measurement. The score is 2 and not 3 because neither reviewer says in words that rapid trigger was on during the 2.4 GHz test, and the two measurements exist for one board only.
decides: It confirms the Gamakay TK75 TMR (a board we link) as the pick for someone who wants rapid trigger off the cable. Two reviewers measured its 2.4 GHz mode within 0.15 ms (HLPlanet) and 0.39 ms (Vortex Gaming) of wired, and both list 8,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz, whereas ChatGPT's Attack Shark example drops to 1,000 Hz wireless. It does not prove rapid trigger itself stays active on 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth; that needs the maker's statement from another angle. No measurement was found for the Gamakay TK75HE V2 or NS75, so this angle cannot rank them.
